summary: Bounded transactional outbox poller scheduler-policy seam for repeated worker cycles.
claim_boundary: Scheduler-policy seam only. This slice adds a deterministic bounded poller loop over an injected worker-cycle runner with max ticks, idle shutdown, consecutive-error shutdown, and capped error backoff. It performs no sleeping, process spawning, live database I/O, live broker/gRPC I/O, process supervision, deployment, or production delivery guarantee.

facets.F1_simplicity: The poller crate owns only stop/backoff/counting policy over an injected runner instead of embedding SQLx, broker, gRPC, process, or timer dependencies.
facets.F2_hyperscaler: The bounded loop prepares future horizontally scaled publisher daemons by making idle shutdown, error shutdown, capped backoff, per-tick outcomes, and aggregate counts deterministic and testable before runtime wiring.
facets.F3_adversarial: Tests cover invalid zero/inverted config, idle shutdown, work resetting idle/error streaks, max-tick completion, consecutive-error shutdown, capped exponential backoff, and overflow-resistant backoff calculation.
facets.F5_quality: Focused poller tests plus the 40-package backbone check/test/clippy/fmt matrix, cargo-deny, license-policy, cargo-prefix, catalog/data-class known-blocker probes, parse/config validation, dependency-seam, honest-claims, and diff hygiene are part of this run.
facets.F7_security_privacy: The poller reports only operational counts, tick outcomes, planned delays, and error refs; it adds no payload bodies or raw message/mail/post content and does not touch database or network credentials.
facets.F11_observability: OutboxPollerRunReport and per-tick reports expose stop reason, work/idle/error outcome, planned delay, claimed/published/dead-letter totals, and total runner errors for future daemon telemetry correlation.
